subject: general
question: What physical quantity is obtained by multiplying the velocity of an object by the time it travels, assuming the object moves with a uniform velocity?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Displacement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Displacement** is defined as the shortest distance between the initial and final positions of an object, along with its direction.
 
• When an object moves with a **uniform velocity**, the product of velocity and time gives the displacement of the object.
 
• **Formula:** Displacement (s) = Velocity (v) × Time (t). This is derived from the basic equation of motion when acceleration is zero.
 
• The **SI unit** of displacement is the same as distance, which is the meter (m).
 
• In this case, since the velocity is uniform and there is no change in direction, the displacement will equal the distance covered by the object.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Acceleration**:

 
 
• Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity of an object with respect to time.
 
• It is calculated using the formula: Acceleration (a) = Change in velocity (Δv) / Time (t).
 
• Its **SI unit** is meters per second squared (m/s²).
 
• It is not obtained by multiplying velocity with time.
 
 
 
• **Momentum**:
 
 
• Momentum is the product of an object's mass (m) and its velocity (v).
 
• Formula: Momentum (p) = Mass (m) × Velocity (v).
 
• Its **SI unit** is kilogram meter per second (kg·m/s).
 
• It is unrelated to the product of velocity and time.
 
 
 
• **Force**:
 
 
• Force is the interaction that, when unopposed, changes the motion of an object.
 
• It is calculated using Newton's second law: Force (F) = Mass (m) × Acceleration (a).
 
• Its **SI unit** is the Newton (N).
 
• Force is not derived from the product of velocity and time.
 
 
 
• **Displacement Features**:
 
 
• Displacement is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude and direction.
 
• For example, if an object moves 5 meters east, its displacement is 5 meters in the east direction.
 
• Displacement can be zero if the object returns to its starting point.
 
• It is different from distance, which is a scalar quantity and only measures the path traveled.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Uniform Velocity:**

 
 
• When an object moves with a constant speed in a straight line, its velocity is uniform.
 
• Under uniform velocity, displacement is directly proportional to time.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Distance and Displacement:**
 
 
• **Distance:** Total path traveled, scalar quantity, always positive.
 
• **Displacement:** Shortest path between two points, vector quantity, can be positive, negative, or zero.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Displacement is crucial in physics for motion analysis in both linear and rotational mechanics.
 
• It is used in navigation, robotics, and engineering to determine exact positioning.
